title: Automated Research Budget Guardrails
business: Financial analysts performing automated market research using AI agents.
problem: Unbounded agent loops can lead to excessive API costs or infinite reasoning cycles when research tasks become overly complex or ambiguous.
solution: Implementing a MaxTurnsExceeded termination condition via the runner configuration to force-stop agents after a predefined number of interaction cycles.
steps: Define an Agent instance with specific research instructions.
Initialize a RunConfig object with a strict max_turns integer value.
Execute the agent using the Runner class passing the custom RunConfig.
Catch the MaxTurnsExceeded exception in the application logic to handle budget-exhausted states.
Log the final state of the agent for audit and manual review.
outcome: Predictable resource consumption and prevention of runaway agent costs during complex research tasks.
limitation: The MaxTurnsExceeded limit is a hard stop that may interrupt valid, long-running research; developers must check if the agent reached a natural conclusion before the limit.

code.content:
from agents import Agent, Runner, RunConfig
# Define agent with research goal
agent = Agent(name="Researcher", instructions="Analyze market trends.")
# Configure max turns to prevent infinite loops
config = RunConfig(max_turns=5)
# Run with explicit limit
try:
    result = await Runner.run(agent, "Analyze sector X", run_config=config)
except MaxTurnsExceeded:
    # Handle budget exhaustion
    print("Research stopped: budget exhausted.")
code.explanation: This code demonstrates setting a hard limit on agent interactions to ensure the Automated Research Budget Guardrails are enforced.
